title: text paragraphs 2
content:
At the center of the dispute is Micron's Incentive Pay Plan (IPP), which the union says lacks transparency and is part of a compensation system that disproportionately rewards senior executives and compares unfavorably with those of Micron's competitors.

The union is seeking a long-term system under which 15 percent of Micron's operating profit would be distributed to employees.

"What we want is to establish an open and transparent profit-sharing system," Lin said.

In September, Micron announced a package under which Taiwan employees would receive at least NT$1.7 million in cash compensation for the fiscal year 2026. This was rejected by the union, which said it would continue to push for a permanent, institutionalized profit-sharing system instead of a one-time measure.

The union is also encouraging employees to take leave and join a rally on Ketagalan Boulevard in Taipei on Monday, Oct. 19.

Micron reported on Sept. 30 that it had US$133.19 billion in revenue and US$99.34 billion in operating income for fiscal 2026, which ended Sept. 3.

Meanwhile, Micron's Taichung union will hold a second mediation session with the company on Oct. 22 before deciding its next step.

Micron has 12,300 employees in Taichung, including approximately 11,000 union members, while Taoyuan has around 3,000 employees, about 2,400 of whom are union members.
